title: Count ten tablets out of a stock bottle on a pill counting tray
instruction: Count out exactly 10 tablets from the stock bottle: pour some onto the counting tray's floor and slide them into the tray's trough with the spatula until exactly 10 are in, then close the trough's lid. Leave every other tablet in the stock bottle or on the counting floor, and screw the bottle's cap back on. Never pour a tablet straight into the trough, touch one with a gripper, or let one fall onto the counter.
context: Pharmacy technicians and pharmacists (about 470,000 and 330,000 US jobs) count tablets by hand on a counting tray many times a day. They open the stock bottle, pour some tablets onto the tray and slide them into the tray's trough a few at a time with a spatula until the count is reached, then close the trough's lid and recap the stock bottle. Afterwards the counted tablets go from the trough's spout into the prescription vial. No tablet is touched by hand, and the count must be exact. This task is the count, from opening the bottle to closing the lid and recapping; only tablets the spatula slides from the counting floor into the trough count.
setup:
A pharmacy dispensing counter (the station table) in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. Behind the counter's back edge stands a white steel pharmacy shelving unit (two 36 in sections, 12 in deep, 84 in tall) full of stock bottles (fixed, out of reach). On the counter:
(1) A 100-count stock bottle: a white HDPE round packer, 150 cc, 53.3 mm across (a 1 mm wall, 51.3 mm inside) and 93.0 mm tall to the top of its 38-400 neck (37.6 mm over the thread, a 31.0 mm bore), 17 g, with a white and blue label; 16 tablets in it. It stands 17 cm forward and 5 cm left, closed by
(2) its plain (not child-resistant) white PP 38-400 screw cap, 40.5 mm across and 15 mm tall, 4 g: one turn of thread at 6 per inch (4.2 mm per turn); it takes 1.0 N m to break loose and 0.3 N m to keep turning.
(3) The tablets: 16 white Smarties Original candy tablets (Smarties Candy Company), inert stand-ins for 10 mm round tablets: compressed dextrose discs about 10 mm across and 4 mm thick, 0.49 g each (a 7.35 g roll holds 15), all alike. The same 16 are used in every trial (handling in the reset notes).
(4) A right-handed pill counting tray, light-blue plastic, 21.2 x 14.9 cm and 3.8 cm tall, 100 g, its middle 25.5 cm forward and 6.5 cm right: a flat counting floor 1.95 cm up, inside 1.85 cm walls at the left and back and a 6 mm lip at the front. Down its right side runs a trough (a half-tube 32 mm across inside, its rim level with the floor, with a 2.5 mm rib along the floor's edge) under a blue hinged lid (a half-tube, 12 g) that stands open at 110 degrees. The trough narrows at its far end into a spout 2.5 cm long and 1.8 cm wide. At the near-left corner the floor runs on into a return spout 3 cm long, narrowing to 2.2 cm. A 1 cm spatula slot runs along the outside of its left wall.
(5) In the slot, standing on its edge, a stainless-steel counting spatula: a 127 mm blade, 19 mm wide and 0.8 mm thick, with a round tip, on a 100 mm wooden handle 19 x 11 mm, 30 g; the handle points toward the robot.
The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring:
Judged on where every tablet is, after every control step (0.05 s). In the bottle: its centre inside the bottle. In the trough: inside the tray's trough or its spout. On the counting floor: over the tray's floor or its return spout. Down: outside the bottle and the tray, its centre at most 1.2 cm over the counter. Counted in by the spatula: a tablet enters the trough straight from the counting floor, where it has lain at least 1 s, the spatula pushed it within the last 1 s (the blade touched it, directly or through a chain of touching tablets), and the tray is within 5 degrees of level. Every entry is checked; a tablet that leaves the trough loses its count, and coming back in needs a new push of the spatula.
0.0 for the whole trial (latched, never reset) if a tablet is ever down; if any part of either arm ever touches a tablet (any contact force over 0.0001 N, a 48th of its weight); or if a tablet ever enters the trough any other way (poured or dropped from the bottle, bounced in, tipped in, pushed by anything but the spatula). Otherwise, at the end, if the bottle was opened (its cap unscrewed off), exactly 10 tablets are in the trough, each counted in by the spatula and lying inside the trough's tube (none resting on top of the lid), and every other tablet is in the bottle or on the counting floor: 1.0 with the trough's lid shut (within 3 degrees of closed; it reads 0.0 shut, and a tablet under its edge holds it 6.1 open, computed) and the bottle's cap screwed back down (turned at least 300 degrees after its thread caught, within 0.6 mm of its seat); 0.5 with the lid shut; 0.25 with the lid open. Else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit or once the full score has held 1 s with everything still.
In a real trial: (a) after the run, open the lid and count the tablets in the trough (10), then those in the bottle and on the counting floor (6). (b) The spatula count, from the overhead camera's video stepped frame by frame from the first stroke to the lid closing: at each frame where a tablet crosses the trough's inner rim, check that it had lain still on the counting floor before that stroke and that the blade was pushing it (touching it or the tablets in front of it) within the 1 s before it crossed. Tally the crossings: in minus out must equal 10. A crossing that fails either check (a tablet poured or dropped from the bottle, bounced in, tipped in by lifting the tray, or pushed by a finger or the bottle) scores 0. (c) The photo and the three videos show no tablet on the counter or the floor, no gripper touching a tablet, and the tray flat on the counter during the count. (d) The lid lies flat on the trough with nothing under its edge; the cap is screwed down when it stops turning with its skirt at the neck's ledge.
reset_notes: Put all 16 tablets back in the stock bottle (tip the trough's ten out of its spout into it) and screw its cap down. Stand the bottle and the tray where they were, open the trough's lid fully (it rests at 110 degrees) and stand the spatula in its slot with the handle toward the robot. Tablets: set them out with clean dry gloves, keep them dry in the closed bottle between trials, replace any chipped one from a new roll, and use a fresh set of 16 white Smarties each day. Wipe the tray, spatula and bottle with a dry cloth after a session.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control), real sizes and masses. Tablets are flat discs (friction 0.25). The cap's thread is a joint (4.2 mm per turn; 1.0 N m to break loose, then 0.3 N m). Hidden linings stop fast tablets passing thin walls: the bottle body's 51.3 mm inside collides 45.1 mm wide (the 31.0 mm neck bore is unlined); its floor collides 3 mm and the tray's 10 mm thicker. Contacts are read every 0.05 s. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
